item.title: North Lynn mechanic banned after A17 traffic stop
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
North Lynn mechanic banned after A17 traffic stop
A North Lynn mechanic has been disqualified from driving for six months following an incident on the A17. Police stopped 39-year-old Jevgenijus Levinskas on April 20 after noticing he was driving a vehicle insured to someone else. Officers discovered Levinskas was using false number plates to conceal the fact that he did not hold a valid driving licence. A search of the car also uncovered a quantity of the Class B drug Cathinone. At Lynn Magistrates’ Court, Levinskas pleaded guilty to multiple driving offences and drug possession. He was issued a £120 fine and received six penalty points, resulting in a driving ban after exceeding the 12-point limit.

item.title: North Lynn pair deny animal neglect charges
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
North Lynn pair deny animal neglect charges
Two people from North Lynn have appeared at Lynn Magistrates’ Court to deny charges of causing prolonged neglect to a dog. Mark Ogle, aged 35, and 41-year-old Jade Kennett, both of Walpole Road, entered not guilty pleas regarding an incident alleged to have occurred on June 25.
Ms Kennett also denied a separate charge of using threatening words to cause alarm or distress on June 24. The case has been adjourned until January 7 to allow for further communication between the Crown Prosecution Service and the RSPCA. Mr Ogle has been released on unconditional bail, while Ms Kennett remains on bail with conditions preventing her from contacting the alleged victim of the threatening behaviour.

item.title: Three-year driving ban for King’s Lynn drug-driver
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Three-year driving ban for King’s Lynn drug-driver
A 35-year-old man from King’s Lynn has been disqualified from driving for three years after testing positive for cannabis. Harry Burt, of Persimmon in Fairstead, was stopped by police on Queensway in Gaywood while driving without insurance. A roadside test revealed he had double the legal limit of THC in his system.
At Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Burt pleaded guilty to drug-driving, driving without insurance, and possession of cannabis. The court heard he had consumed the drug to assist with sleep. In addition to the driving ban, Burt was ordered to pay a total of £634 in fines, costs, and a victim surcharge.

item.title: Police appeal following King’s Lynn hit-and-run
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Police appeal following King’s Lynn hit-and-run
Norfolk Police are appealing for witnesses after a collision in King’s Lynn on Wednesday evening. At approximately 5pm, a black Porsche was observed weaving through traffic on London Road before striking a grey MG. The driver of the Porsche failed to stop at the scene and left the area.
Fortunately, no injuries were reported following the incident. Officers are now working to trace the driver involved. Anyone who witnessed the collision or has relevant information is asked to contact Norfolk Police quoting reference 1837166. Details can also be provided anonymously through Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.
